text: Q: How long is a million seconds? A: About 11½ days.
Q: How long is a billion seconds? A: About 31.7 years.
Q: How long is a trillion seconds? A: About 31,700 years.
A year is about π × 10⁷ seconds — accurate to within half a percent.
A million minutes is about 1.9 years. A billion minutes is about 1,900 years.
Your heart beats roughly a billion times every 27 years.
Your heart beats a million times in about 10 days.
By age 81, your heart has beaten about 3 billion times.
You take about a million breaths every 43 days.
Your heart pumps about 7,200 litres of blood a day — roughly 48 bathtubs.
Over 80 years, your heart pumps enough blood to fill about 84 Olympic pools.
At 7,500 steps a day for 80 years, you would walk around Earth 4.4 times.
In an 80-year life, you spend roughly 27 years asleep.
All your DNA stretched out could reach the Sun and back about 250 times.
Spend $1,000 a day and a billion dollars lasts about 2,738 years.
A million steps is roughly 500 miles of walking.
A million hours is about 114 years.
Light takes 1.3 seconds to reach us from the Moon, and 8 minutes 20 seconds from the Sun.
